zh: 答案就是 N 与最近的二进制回文数之间的距离。固定位数后，回文数由前半部分唯一决定，而且数值随前半部分严格递增。
所以对每个位数，只需检查由 N 的高位前缀 p 以及 p−1、p+1 镜像得到的回文（限制在该位数的合法前缀范围内），再加上该位数最小和最大的回文，覆盖跨位数的情况。N<2³¹，位数枚举 1 到 31 即可。
best 初值为 N（0 本身是回文）；对 bits=1..31：half=⌈bits/2⌉，合法前缀范围 [2^(half−1), 2^half−1]，p=N 右移 ⌊bits/2⌋ 位；对候选前缀 {下界, 上界, clamp(p), clamp(p−1), clamp(p+1)}，把前缀拼上自身（奇数位时去掉最后一位）的反转得到回文，用 |回文−N| 更新 best；输出 best。
en: The answer is the distance from N to the nearest binary palindrome. For a fixed bit length, a palindrome is uniquely determined by its first half, and its value increases strictly with that half.

So for each length it is enough to check the palindromes mirrored from N's high prefix p and from p-1 and p+1 (clamped to that length's valid prefix range), plus the smallest and largest palindromes of that length to cover crossing a length boundary. N < 2^31, so lengths 1 to 31 suffice.

Start best at N (0 is itself a palindrome); for bits = 1..31: half = ceil(bits/2), the valid prefix range is [2^(half-1), 2^half - 1], and p = N shifted right by floor(bits/2); for each candidate prefix in {lower end, upper end, clamp(p), clamp(p-1), clamp(p+1)}, append the reverse of the prefix (dropping its last bit when bits is odd) to form the palindrome and update best with |palindrome - N|; print best.

explanationEn:
## Approach

Enumerate target binary palindromes by bit length. For a fixed length, the second half of the palindrome is the mirror of the first half. Let p be the high prefix of N; the nearest candidates of that length only require checking p and its neighbouring prefixes (clamped to the valid range for that length). Also check the smallest and largest palindromes of that length to cover crossing a length boundary. Enumerate candidates of 1 to 31 bits and take the smallest absolute difference from N.

## Correctness

For a fixed length, valid binary palindromes correspond one-to-one to their first halves, and their values increase strictly with the first half. The best distance from a candidate palindrome to N only changes when the prefix crosses the prefix corresponding to N, so checking the neighbouring prefixes gives the nearest value within that length; both ends of the valid prefix range are also checked. N is at most 2 * 10^9, less than 2^31, so the nearest palindrome must have between 1 and 31 bits. Taking the minimum difference over all lengths gives the minimum number of increment/decrement operations.

## Complexity

At most 31 lengths are enumerated and each checks a constant number of candidates; time O(log N), extra space O(1).

## Sources and site conventions

The Python, Java and C++ implementations of the fixed OAMaster snapshot all add or subtract integers and check whether the standard binary representation is a palindrome; the original example N = 6 has answer 1. The snapshot constraint is 0 <= N <= 2 * 10^9. The input/output format is an addition by this site. Source: https://oamaster.com/docs/companies/google#56-minimum-operations-to-make-binary-palindromic
